question.text: A commodity user (processor) who needs to buy raw materials in the future should adopt:

answer.text: A long hedge — buy futures to lock in the purchase price
A short hedge — sell futures to lock in the purchase price
No hedge — wait for prices to fall naturally
A spread trade between two different commodities

explanation.text: The Logic: Commodity users/processors buy raw materials and can lock in the purchase price using a long hedge — buying futures for a future acquisition. If prices rise, the futures gain offsets the higher spot purchase cost. The Trap: Short hedges are for sellers (producers). No hedge leaves the processor exposed. Spread trades between different commodities do not directly hedge purchase costs. Note: The source describes a processor locking the raw-material purchase price for stocks to be used over the next 3 to 6 months.
